a1.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James positions itself through AdvisorChoice®, a platform of multiple affiliation options (traditional employee, Advisor Select, independent contractor, bank & credit union, corporate RIA, RIA & custody services), each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility backed by a leading independent firm.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that's right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility – and all backed by the full support of a leading independent financial firm.

items.text: The firm describes its value proposition as a 'best-of-both-worlds' combination of an advisor and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, with a strong balance sheet and commitment to independence as a differentiator.
items.quote: Our best-of-both-worlds value proposition, where we offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, continues to resonate with advisors across all of our affiliation options. Additionally, our strong balance sheet and commitment to independence is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

items.text: Raymond James says it has the largest addressable market across its affiliation options (employee to independent contractor to RIA custody) with critical mass and decades of experience in all of them, and that this value proposition, cultural fit and platform appeal to advisors from many different firms, not just one.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market across our affiliation options, from employee to independent contractor to the RIA custody, and we have critical mass and decades of experience in all of them... that value proposition, the cultural fit, the platform that I talked about, the multiple affiliation options, it's appealing to advisors from a lot of different firms.

items.text: The firm states it does not lead with the highest check but with culture and capabilities, offering a differentiated value proposition rather than competing primarily on economics/transition assistance.
items.quote: we don't lead with the highest check. We want to have competitive economics. Certainly, we have to have competitive economics, but we lead with culture and capabilities. And so we have a true differentiated value proposition.

items.text: Raymond James attributes its ability to attract high-quality advisors to its values-based culture, commitment to service, and the unique ways it provides services to financial advisors.
items.quote: Our ability to attract high quality advisors is based on our values-based culture, our commitment to service, and the unique ways in which we provide services to our financial advisors.

items.text: The firm frames its positioning as advisors not having to choose between culture and capabilities: a unique combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture along with leading technology, products and solutions needed to serve clients at a high level.
items.quote: advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture along with the leading technology, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level.

a1.RJF.reason: Multiple passages directly describe how Raymond James positions itself to recruit advisors, including its affiliation options, culture-and-capabilities value proposition, and differentiation from wirehouse-style competition.

a2.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James & Associates, the firm's employee advisor channel, added the Le Sage Mattiza Maggard Wealth Management team, which previously managed more than $550 million in client assets at UBS Financial Services, a wirehouse.
items.quote: Operating as Le Sage Mattiza Maggard Wealth Management of Raymond James in The Woodlands, Texas, the team previously managed more than $550 million in client assets at UBS Financial Services.

items.text: Raymond James brought on breakaway teams from wirehouses Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley whose combined client assets exceeded $1 billion.
items.quote: Earlier this year, the firm brought on breakaway teams from Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley whose combined assets exceeded $1 billion

items.text: Raymond James & Associates has maintained a consistent run of recruiting advisors from UBS throughout 2026, as advisors at the wirehouse respond to changes in how the firm compensates its advisor workforce.
items.quote: The Ohio hire extends a consistent run of Raymond James & Associates recruiting from UBS throughout 2026 , as advisors at the wirehouse continue to respond to changes in how the firm compensates its advisor workforce.

a2.RJF.reason: The firm's own disclosures aggregate recruiting production and assets across all sources without separating wirehouse-sourced advisors, but trade press passages report specific wirehouse recruits (from UBS, Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley) with client asset figures, which I report as facts.

a3.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James describes its value proposition to prospective advisors as a combination of an advisor- and client-focused culture together with leading technology, products and solutions, plus a strong balance sheet and commitment to independence, so that advisors 'do not have to choose between culture and capabilities.'
items.quote: At Raymond James, advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture together with leading technologies, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level. Combined with our strong balance sheet, long-term thinking and commitment to independence, that continues to set Raymond James apart for advisers evaluating alternatives.

items.text: The firm states it does not lead recruiting with the highest check but with culture and capabilities, remaining disciplined on transition assistance and economics, while still offering competitive economics.
items.quote: we don't lead with the highest check. We want to have competitive economics. Certainly, we have to have competitive economics, but we lead with culture and capabilities... we remain disciplined. We've always been disciplined on those transaction assistance -- transition assistance and economics to advisers.

items.text: Raymond James offers payout structures by affiliation model: up to 50% payout for Traditional Employee, 70-80% gross payout for Advisor Select, and 81% to 90% payout for Independent Contractor.
items.quote: Model: Traditional Employee... Up to 50% payout** and full array of competitive employee benefits offerings. ... Model: Advisor Select... 70-80% gross payout** ... Model: Independent Contractor... 81% to 90% payout***.

items.text: The firm offers loans to financial advisors originated as part of its recruiting activities as a form of transition/incentive package.
items.quote: Loans to financial advisors are primarily comprised of loans originated as a part of our recruiting activities.

items.text: The firm notes it would rather recruit advisors one by one so that 100% of transition assistance paid goes to retention of the advisor rather than to a seller, as would occur in an acquisition.
items.quote: we'd much rather recruit one by one, where we know the advisors are a good cultural fit, and 100% of what we pay in transition assistance is going to retention versus the seller.

items.text: Raymond James has designed a compensation structure including competitive pay packages (base salary, incentive bonus, equity compensation), annual ESOP and profit-sharing contributions, 401(k) matching, an employee stock purchase plan at a discount, and non-qualified deferred compensation plans, intended to attract current and prospective associates.
items.quote: Our competitive pay packages include base salary, incentive bonus, and equity compensation programs. Additionally, the firm makes annual contributions to support the retirement goals of each associate through our employee stock ownership plan and our profit-sharing plan, in addition to a matching contribution program for the 401(k)... an employee stock purchase plan that enables them to acquire our common stock at a discount... we also offer various non-qualified deferred compensation plans.

items.text: The firm notes the industry is competitive, with other firms offering guaranteed contracts, upfront payments, and increased compensation, and that Raymond James may offer loans or other incentives to newly recruited financial advisors.
items.quote: other firms are offering guaranteed contracts, upfront payments, and increased compensation. Our financial results may be adversely affected by the costs we incur in connection with any loans or other incentives we may offer to newly recruited financial advisors and other key personnel.

items.text: The firm cites its value proposition of a unique combination of advisor- and client-focused culture coupled with leading technology and solutions, plus a strong balance sheet and commitment to independence, as a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives, supported by investments such as the private wealth advisor program and expanded alternatives platform.
items.quote: We offer a unique combination of an advisor and client-focused culture, coupled with leading technology and solutions. This value proposition, coupled with our strong balance sheet and commitment to independence, is proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives.

items.text: The firm emphasizes advisor book ownership as part of its employee value proposition ('It's your business. Your brand. Your clients.'), with no quotas or product pushing.
items.quote: True partnership. We've redefined the employee advisor experience, enabled by advisor book ownership. It's your business. Your brand. Your clients... you're free to succeed on your terms – no quotas, no product pushing.

a3.RJF.reason: Multiple passages state the firm's value proposition, competitive economics/discipline on transition assistance, payout structures, transition loans, and compensation/benefits packages offered to attract advisors.

a4.RJF.label: fact

items.text: As of September 30, 2025 (fiscal 2025 year-end), Raymond James had 8,943 total financial advisors.
items.quote: Employees 3,878 3,826 3,693 / Independent contractors 5,065 4,961 5,019 / Total advisors 8,943 8,787 8,712

items.quote: As of September 30, 2025, we had approximately 19,500 associates (including 3,878 employee financial advisors) and 5,065 independent advisors.

items.text: The number of financial advisors as of September 30, 2025 increased compared to the prior year, as new recruits and trainees moved into production roles exceeded departures and planned retirements.

items.text: Raymond James ended fiscal 2025 with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year, a reflection of solid advisor retention as well as strong recruiting results.
items.quote: We ended the fiscal year with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year, and a reflection of solid advisor retention as well as strong recruiting results.

a5.RJF.label: fact

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry stated that as the firm enters the fiscal fourth quarter, it does so with significant momentum supported by robust financial adviser recruiting and strong investment banking pipelines.
items.quote: As we enter the fiscal fourth quarter, we do so with significant momentum, supported by historically strong business drivers, robust financial adviser recruiting and strong investment banking pipelines, along with ample capital and liquidity to support continued growth.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry described the recruiting pipeline as strong and broad-based, not driven by one firm, one catalyst, or one affiliation option, and noted net new assets for the fiscal year were up 119% to $75 billion.
items.quote: we're one of those firms, and we couple that with the capabilities and that's what's really driven our strong recruiting results and the pipeline remains strong. This is not a pipeline that is driven by one firm or one catalyst in the market or one affiliation option.

items.text: Trade press reported a consistent run of Raymond James & Associates recruiting from UBS throughout 2026, as advisors at the wirehouse respond to changes in how the firm compensates its advisor workforce.
items.quote: The Ohio hire extends a consistent run of Raymond James & Associates recruiting from UBS throughout 2026 , as advisors at the wirehouse continue to respond to changes in how the firm compensates its advisor workforce.

items.text: Trade press reported that Raymond James & Associates welcomed Adam E. Pearsall to its employee advisor channel from UBS Financial Services, where he managed more than $400 million in client assets.
items.quote: Raymond James & Associates welcomed Adam E. Pearsall, CFP, to its employee advisor channel from UBS Financial Services, where he managed more than $400 million in client assets.

a5.RJF.reason: The passages contain recent statements by the CEO on recruiting pipeline and momentum, and trade-press reports of new wirehouse (UBS) advisor hires.

a6.RJF.label: fact

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry states Raymond James has a 97% adviser satisfaction rate, which he describes as the best he knows of in the industry compared with other CEOs and firms, and that this retention is the foundation for growth.
items.quote: we have 97% adviser satisfaction rate, 97% adviser satisfaction rate with our surveys, which is the best I know of in the industry when I speak to other CEOs and other firms. And so that retention is the foundation for the growth.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry states Raymond James has the largest addressable market in the industry because it offers all the affiliation options an adviser could want, and that this combination is increasingly unique in the industry.
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market in the industry because we have all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want. And we have adviser choice where we're agnostic into how you affiliate with Raymond James.

items.text: For fiscal year 2025, Raymond James recruited financial advisors to its domestic independent contractor and employee channels with trailing 12-month production totaling $407 million, a 21% increase over the prior year's previous record.
items.quote: In fiscal year 2025, we had record recruiting results of financial advisors to our domestic independent contractor and employee channels, with recruiting trailing 12-month production at their previous firms totaling $407 million, reflecting a 21% increase over last year's previous record.
items.scope: domestic independent contractor and employee channels

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry states the fiscal second quarter recruited production and assets was the second highest quarterly result in the firm's history, comparing to prior quarters.
items.quote: We recruited financial advisers to our domestic independent contractor and employee channels, with trailing 12-month production totaling $141 million, nearly $21 billion of client assets at their previous firms. The second highest quarterly result in our history in terms of both recruited production and assets.

items.text: Trade press reports the Ohio hire extends a consistent run of Raymond James & Associates recruiting from UBS throughout 2026, as wirehouse advisors respond to changes in how that firm compensates its advisor workforce.
items.quote: The Ohio hire extends a consistent run of Raymond James & Associates recruiting from UBS throughout 2026 , as advisors at the wirehouse continue to respond to changes in how the firm compensates its advisor workforce.

items.text: Trade press reports Raymond James has been one of the most significant beneficiaries of teams looking to leave Commonwealth ahead of its conversion to LPL, and that the firm has boosted its recruitment spending over the past year.
items.quote: Raymond James has been one of the most significant beneficiaries of teams looking to leave Commonwealth ahead of the conversion, and the firm has boosted its recruitment spending over the past year, according to earnings reports.

items.quote: Earlier this year, the firm brought on breakaway teams from Wells Fargo and Morgan Stanley whose combined assets exceeded $1 billion, and it added a $420 million Edward Jones team in Virginia late last year.

Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2024 (fiscal 2024 year-end), Raymond James had 8,787 total financial advisors.
Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2023 (fiscal 2023 year-end), Raymond James had 8,712 total financial advisors.
Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2025, Raymond James had 3,878 employee financial advisors and 5,065 independent advisors.

Raymond James Financial: The number of financial advisors as of September 30, 2025 increased compared to the prior year, as new recruits and trainees moved into production roles exceeded departures and planned retirements.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended September 30, 2025, management said the firm ended fiscal 2025 with a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year, a reflection of solid advisor retention as well as strong recruiting results.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended June 30, 2026, CEO Paul Shoukry stated that as the firm enters the fiscal fourth quarter it does so with significant momentum, supported by robust financial adviser recruiting and strong investment banking pipelines. Why it might matter: the source states this momentum follows record revenues, record pre-tax income and record earnings per share in the first nine months of the fiscal year.

Raymond James Financial: On the earnings call for the period ended June 30, 2026, CEO Paul Shoukry described the recruiting pipeline as strong and broad-based, not driven by one firm, one catalyst, or one affiliation option, and noted net new assets for the fiscal year were up 119% to $75 billion. Why it might matter: the source states the pipeline draws advisers from many different firms and communities interested in all of the firm's affiliation options, and management says it does not think the pipeline is idiosyncratic.

Raymond James Financial: The comparison can be made only qualitatively, not as a ranked quantitative comparison across firms on a shared basis. The evidence consists of management's own characterizations relative to the industry (a 97% adviser satisfaction rate described as the best the CEO knows of in the industry, and the largest addressable market in the industry), its own prior periods (the fiscal second quarter recruited production and assets being the second highest quarterly result in the firm's history), and trade-press characterizations (a consistent run of recruiting from UBS in 2026, and being one of the most significant beneficiaries of teams leaving Commonwealth ahead of its conversion to LPL), rather than comparable figures across firms on a common basis.

a1.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states it has built its adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed, through a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology and dedicated service and support.
items.quote: We have built our adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed. Today, we serve more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets with a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology and dedicated service and support.

items.text: Schwab states its strategy is to maintain its competitive position primarily through the efforts of its sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams, which are dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients, plus a highly-developed, scalable platform to administer clients' assets easily and efficiently.
items.quote: Management believes that we can maintain our competitive position primarily through the efforts of our sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams, which are dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed in serving their clients. In addition to focusing on superior service, we utilize technology to provide RIAs with a highly-developed, scalable platform for administering their clients' assets easily and efficiently.

items.text: Schwab states it is deepening relationships with the RIA firms it serves by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs.
items.quote: we're deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms we serve by building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone to add value for RIAs.

items.text: Schwab describes its goal as providing the leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment/lending products, and technology in addition to custody and service.
items.quote: The leading RIA support ecosystem to help advisors serve their clients, providing wealth tools, investment / lending products, & technology in addition to custody & service

items.text: Schwab lists 'Broaden support for RIAs while improving monetization' as one of its strategic priorities under 'Serve More Clients & Deepen Relationships'.
items.quote: Broaden support for RIAs while improving monetization

a1.MER.label: fact

items.text: Merrill's advisor growth strategy centers on adding financial advisors to the sales force through its extensive training program and through experienced hiring of advisors, with about one-third of net new households added by newly trained advisors.
items.quote: We also continued to add financial advisors to the sales force in Merrill and the Private Bank through our extensive training program and experienced hiring of advisors. Approximately one-third of net new households in Q2 were added by our newly trained advisors.

items.text: Management describes experienced advisor recruiting as 'not an enormous part' of the strategy, with the core being a training program that trains people in wealth management at Bank of America and Merrill to keep driving net new flows.
items.quote: we're picking up the recruiting of experienced advisors. That isn't an enormous part of our strategy, but it's a training program so that we're training people in wealth management, Bank of America, and Merrill, and that's ultimately what we believe we can just keep driving in order to improve the net new flows.

items.text: Merrill's Advisor Development Program progresses advisors through roles—ADP Client Associate, ADP Financial Solutions Advisor, then ADP Financial Advisor—until they graduate to Merrill Core Advisor.
items.quote: After mastering key objectives and pre-determined targets, progress through three roles until you graduate to Merrill Core Advisor.

items.text: Merrill states a foundational belief that having the best advisors enables it to deliver exceptional client outcomes.
items.quote: having the best advisors enables us to deliver exceptional client outcomes

items.text: Management's stated objective is to keep growing the sales force, noting advisor attrition is now at near historic lows.
items.quote: what Lindsay and Eric are trying to drive there, what Katy is trying to drive there is just keep growing the sales force. Well, adviser attrition is now at near historic lows.

items.text: Merrill continues to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers and is driving productivity higher on both newer and existing advisers.
items.quote: We're driving productivity higher on both newer and existing members of our financial advisers team, and we continue to attract talent across both new and experienced advisers.

items.text: Merrill returned to veteran (experienced) broker recruiting after largely pulling back from it at the end of 2017, restoring a focus on hiring with a more aggressive offer under Co-Presidents who took over in 2023.
items.quote: The firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 but returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer.

a1.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James offers multiple affiliation options, collectively referred to as AdvisorChoice®, through which financial advisors primarily affiliate with the firm directly as employees, as independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.
items.quote: We offer multiple affiliation options, which we refer to as AdvisorChoice®. Financial advisors primarily affiliate with us directly as either employees or independent contractors or as employees of third-party Registered Investment Advisors ("RIAs") and broker-dealers to which we provide services through our RIA and Custody Services ("RCS") division.

items.text: Through AdvisorChoice®, the firm offers a platform of affiliation options — Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, Corporate RIA, and RIA & Custody Services — each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility.
items.quote: Through AdvisorChoice®, you have the ability to match your professional goals to the affiliation option that's right for you, each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility... AdvisorChoice® A platform of dynamic options and the freedom to choose among them. Traditional Employee... Advisor Select... Independent Contractor... Bank & Credit Union... Corporate RIA... RIA & Custody Services...

items.text: The AdvisorChoice spectrum spans Employee (RJA), Advisor Select, Independent Advisor (ICD), Banks and Credit Unions, IAR (Corporate RIA), and RIA & Custody Services, and the firm states the movement to "independence" is not channel-specific.
items.quote: EMPLOYEE INDEPENDENT CONTRACTOR RIA & CUSTODY SERVICES EMPLOYEE ADVISOR (RJA) ADVISOR SELECT INDEPENDENT ADVISOR (ICD) BANKS AND CREDIT UNIONS IAR* (CORPORATE RIA) RIA** & CUSTODY SERVICES... The movement to "independence" is not channel-specific

items.text: Employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff, provide services predominantly to retail clients, and receive compensation primarily as a payout on revenues they generate plus participation in the firm's employee benefit plans.
items.quote: Employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff. They provide services predominantly to retail clients. Compensation for these financial advisors primarily includes a payout on revenues they generate and such advisors also participate in the firm's employee benefit plans.

items.text: Independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and therefore receive a higher payout percentage than employee advisors; they may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in the Financial Institutions Division, and with approval may conduct certain other approved business activities.
items.quote: Our financial advisors who are independent contractors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and, accordingly, receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors... Independent contractor financial advisors may affiliate with us directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in our Financial Institutions Division.

items.text: The firm's affiliation spectrum details payout and qualifications by model: Traditional Employee (up to 50% payout, minimum 5 years experience), Advisor Select (70-80% gross payout, minimum 3 years and $3.5 million annual branch fees and commission revenue), and Independent Contractor (81-90% payout, minimum 3 years).
items.quote: Model: Traditional Employee Qualifications*: Minimum 5 years of experience... Up to 50% payout**... Model: Advisor Select Qualifications*: Minimum 3 years of experience and $3.5 million or higher in annual branch fees and commission revenue. Payout + Benefits: 70-80% gross payout**... Model: Independent Contractor... 81% to 90% payout***.

items.text: Bank & Credit Union, Corporate RIA, and RIA & Custody Services models have their own qualifications and payout structures, including Corporate RIA (81-90% payout, minimum $50 million assets under advisement) and RIA & Custody Services (minimum $100 million to establish a new RIA).
items.quote: Model: Bank & Credit Union Qualifications*: Minimum 3 years of experience and $250,000 in production... Model: Corporate RIA Qualifications*: Minimum 3 years of experience and $50 million in assets under advisement. Payout + Benefits: 81% to 90% payout***... Model: RIA & Custody Services Qualifications*: $100 million or more in assets to establish a new RIA...

items.text: Advisor Select® provides established advisors the full benefits of the employee channel with the independence to create their own branches, letting them run their branch's P&L to earn a higher rate on production.
items.quote: Advisor Select® provides established advisors the full benefits of our employee channel with the independence to create their own branches... run your branch's P&L to earn a higher rate on production.

items.text: The Corporate RIA affiliation model lets fee-based advisors get the RIA experience while streamlining many of its burdens through an all-inclusive affiliation model.
items.quote: Fee-based advisors can get the RIA experience while streamlining many of its burdens with our all-inclusive Corporate RIA affiliation model.

a1.RJF.reason: The passages directly describe Raymond James' multiple affiliation options under the AdvisorChoice® umbrella, including employee, independent contractor, and RIA & Custody Services models and their terms, so these statements are facts.

a2.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James says it is "agnostic" about how advisors affiliate and wants them to "fall in love" with its culture, values, platform and capabilities, and that having all affiliation options gives it "the largest addressable market in the industry."
items.quote: we have the largest addressable market in the industry because we have all the affiliation options that an adviser could possibly want. And we have adviser choice where we're agnostic into how you affiliate with Raymond James. We want you to fall in love with our culture, values and the platform and capabilities and how you affiliate with us, we're indifferent to.

items.text: Raymond James' focus is to "remain the absolute best destination for financial advisers and their clients across all of our affiliation options," which it calls "adviser choice."
items.quote: our focus is just to remain the absolute best destination for financial advisers and their clients across all of our affiliation options. We call it adviser choice

items.text: Raymond James' differentiated value proposition is that "advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities," pairing an advisor- and client-focused culture with leading technology, products and solutions.
items.quote: advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities. We offer a unique combination of an adviser and client-focused culture along with the leading technology, products and solutions advisers need to serve clients at a high level.

items.text: Raymond James lists its strategy pillars as "Multiple Affiliation Options," "Best of Both Worlds," "Advisor and Book Ownership," and "RJF Stability," to "Inspire and empower the world's best financial professionals."
items.quote: Multiple Affiliation Options Best of Both Worlds Advisor and Book Ownership RJF Stability Inspire and empower the world's best financial professionals.

items.text: Raymond James' consistent focus is "being the absolute best destination and firm for financial advisers and their clients and matching that culture with the capabilities that are very hard to find in the marketplace."
items.quote: our focus on being the absolute best destination and firm for financial advisers and their clients and matching that culture with the capabilities that are very hard to find in the marketplace.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry has emphasized the strategy of building Raymond James' advisory ranks through individualized recruitment rather than large-scale acquisitions, evaluating each prospective advisor one-on-one.
items.quote: Shoukry has emphasized the firm's strategy of building its advisory ranks through individualized recruitment rather than large-scale acquisitions, noting that the firm evaluates each prospective advisor on a one-on-one basis.

items.text: Raymond James prefers to "recruit 1 by 1 versus doing acquisitions" because 100% of transition assistance goes to advisor retention and it can ensure recruits are good cultural fits.
items.quote: we prefer to recruit 1 by 1 versus doing acquisitions because we know -- first, 100% of the transition assistance is going to retention of the adviser. And secondly, we can ensure that the advisers we're bringing over a really good cultural fits for the firm.

items.text: Raymond James describes its employee advisor experience as "redefined... enabled by advisor book ownership," with advisors free to succeed on their own terms with "no quotas, no product pushing."
items.quote: We've redefined the employee advisor experience, enabled by advisor book ownership. It's your business. Your brand. Your clients.

items.text: Raymond James seeks to mitigate advisor-departure risk "through financial advisor succession planning and by providing our financial advisors with a broad range of services and resources to support their practices."
items.quote: We seek to mitigate these risks through financial advisor succession planning and by providing our financial advisors with a broad range of services and resources to support their practices.

a2.RJF.reason: Multiple passages state Raymond James' priorities and strategy for its affiliation models (agnostic approach, adviser choice, culture plus capabilities, individualized recruitment, book ownership, succession planning), so these are facts.

a3.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James says private equity-backed roll-ups are a competitive pressure, and that 'in the absence of a value proposition, they compete with big checks.'
items.quote: We are still seeing pressure on the existing advisor base, private equity. We always say with the roll-ups, in the absence of a value proposition, they compete with big checks.

items.text: Raymond James says there are more competitive pressures now from private equity-backed roll-ups.
items.quote: Yeah, there are more competitive pressures now with private equity-backed roll-ups and that sort of thing.

items.text: Raymond James says PE-backed roll-ups have been cropping up everywhere over the last three years and paying increasingly high multiples.
items.quote: The dynamic that's relatively novel in the last five years is these PE-backed roll-ups cropping up everywhere. Over the last three years in particular, they've been extremely aggressive in trading and paying at higher and higher multiples.

items.text: Raymond James contrasts its approach with competitors that are looking for an exit in three to five years, that compete with the largest check, and that change their comp plans every year to cross-sell bank products.
items.quote: so many of our competitors are increasingly looking for an exit in three to five years or even less... many of our competitors compete with the largest check... many of our competitors change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products.

items.text: Raymond James states it competes directly with national full-service broker-dealers, investment banking firms, commercial banks, investment advisors, investment managers, discount brokers and dealers, and more recent entrants including fintechs.
items.quote: We compete directly with other national full service broker-dealers, investment banking firms, commercial banks, investment advisors, investment managers and, to a lesser extent, discount brokers and dealers. We face competition from more recent entrants into the market, including fintechs, and increased use of alternative sales channels by other firms.

items.text: Raymond James identifies the industry-wide trend of financial advisors departing traditional firms to form independent RIAs or join third-party RIAs (some backed by private equity investors) as creating a highly competitive recruiting environment.
items.quote: the continued industry-wide trend in which financial advisors are departing traditional firms, including to form independent RIAs or to join existing third-party RIAs, some of which are backed by private equity investors. This ongoing trend has resulted in a highly competitive recruiting environment.

items.text: Raymond James says private equity has been competitive over the last 5 years, as well as some strategic firms.
items.quote: Private equity has certainly been competitive over the last 5 years as well as some of the strategic firms.

items.text: Raymond James says it does not lead with the highest check, and that competitors lacking a differentiated value proposition must compete on the highest check.
items.quote: we don't lead with the highest check... In the absence of a true differentiated value proposition, the highest check is all you have.

items.text: Raymond James participates (with limited exceptions) in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting and notes that competitors may withdraw from it, and that competitors frequently claim unfair hiring practices.
items.quote: We participate, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting... it is possible that certain of our competitors will withdraw from it. ... companies in our industry whose employees or independent contractors accept positions with competitors frequently claim that those competitors have engaged in unfair hiring practices.

a3.RJF.reason: The passages under a3.RJF contain multiple explicit statements naming the competitive dynamics and competitor types around Raymond James's affiliation models, so all items are labeled fact.

a4.RJF.label: fact

items.text: Raymond James announced it will add $18.7 billion in client assets to its Financial Institutions Division (the unit dedicated to bank and credit union advisors) as an existing FID program merges with Synovus Financial Corp., expanding its relationship with Pinnacle Financial Partners; the advisors are expected to transition in May 2027.
items.quote: Raymond James will add $18.7 billion and 70 advisors to its Financial Institutions Division, the unit dedicated to bank and credit union advisors, as an existing FID program merges with Synovus Financial Corp.

items.text: Raymond James announced it will add 70 advisors to its Financial Institutions Division (the bank and credit union advisor unit) as an existing FID program merges with Synovus Financial Corp.; the advisors are expected to transition in May 2027.
items.quote: Raymond James will add $18.7 billion and 70 advisors to its Financial Institutions Division, the unit dedicated to bank and credit union advisors, as an existing FID program merges with Synovus Financial Corp.

a4.RJF.reason: The passage announces an expansion of the Financial Institutions Division affiliation channel via a merger, which is a change the firm has announced to that affiliation model.

items.text: CEO Paul Shoukry said that over the last year much more of the firm's recruiting has come from the independent side of the business versus the employee side, representing a mix shift.

a6.RJF.reason: Multiple firm statements describe how the mix of recruiting and growth across affiliation models (employee vs independent contractor vs RCS) has shifted over time, with different channels leading in different periods.

claims.text: The 2025 10-K (period ended September 30, 2025, published November 25, 2025) states Raymond James offers multiple affiliation options, which it refers to as AdvisorChoice®, through which financial advisors primarily affiliate with the firm directly as either employees or independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through its RIA and Custody Services (RCS) division.

The firm's affiliation-options web page (content as of April 21, 2026) states that through AdvisorChoice®, the firm offers a platform of affiliation options — Traditional Employee, Advisor Select, Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, Corporate RIA, and RIA & Custody Services — each offering a unique combination of support, freedom and flexibility.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: The 2025 investor-day deck (published June 5, 2025) states the AdvisorChoice spectrum spans Employee Advisor (RJA), Advisor Select, Independent Advisor (ICD), Banks and Credit Unions, IAR (Corporate RIA), and RIA & Custody Services, and that the movement to independence is not channel-specific.

The 2025 10-K states employee financial advisors work in a traditional branch supported by local management and administrative staff, provide services predominantly to retail clients, and receive compensation primarily as a payout on revenues they generate plus participation in the firm's employee benefit plans.

The 2025 10-K states independent contractor financial advisors are generally responsible for all of their direct costs and accordingly receive a higher payout percentage on the revenues they generate than employee financial advisors, may affiliate directly or through an affiliated bank or credit union in the Financial Institutions Division, and with approval may conduct certain other approved business activities.

The firm's affiliation-options web page (content as of April 21, 2026) details payout and qualifications by model: Traditional Employee has up to 50% payout and a minimum of 5 years of experience; Advisor Select has 70-80% gross payout and a minimum of 3 years of experience and $3.5 million or higher in annual branch fees and commission revenue; and Independent Contractor has 81% to 90% payout and a minimum of 3 years of experience.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-04-21 [IR]

claims.text: The firm's affiliation-options web page (content as of April 21, 2026) states the Bank & Credit Union, Corporate RIA, and RIA & Custody Services models have their own qualifications and payout structures, including Corporate RIA at 81% to 90% payout with a minimum of $50 million in assets under advisement, and RIA & Custody Services requiring $100 million or more in assets to establish a new RIA.

claims.text: On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, management said Raymond James is agnostic about how advisors affiliate and wants them to fall in love with its culture, values, platform and capabilities, and that having all the affiliation options gives it the largest addressable market in the industry.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, management said the firm's focus is to remain the absolute best destination for financial advisers and their clients across all of its affiliation options, which it calls adviser choice.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, management said the firm's differentiated value proposition is that advisers do not have to choose between culture and capabilities, offering a unique combination of an adviser- and client-focused culture along with leading technology, products and solutions.

The 2025 investor-day deck (published June 5, 2025) lists the firm's strategy pillars as Multiple Affiliation Options, Best of Both Worlds, Advisor and Book Ownership, and RJF Stability, to inspire and empower the world's best financial professionals.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, management described the firm's consistent focus as being the absolute best destination and firm for financial advisers and their clients and matching that culture with capabilities that are very hard to find in the marketplace.

Trade press (September 29, 2026) reports CEO Paul Shoukry has emphasized the strategy of building Raymond James' advisory ranks through individualized recruitment rather than large-scale acquisitions, evaluating each prospective advisor on a one-on-one basis.

The firm's traditional-employee-advisor web page (content as of May 16, 2026) describes the employee advisor experience as redefined and enabled by advisor book ownership, with advisors free to succeed on their own terms with no quotas and no product pushing.
claims.source_label: RJF press page content as of 2026-05-16 [IR]

claims.text: The 2025 10-K states Raymond James seeks to mitigate advisor-departure risk through financial advisor succession planning and by providing its financial advisors with a broad range of services and resources to support their practices.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2025, management said private equity-backed roll-ups are a competitive pressure, and that in the absence of a value proposition, they compete with big checks.
On the earnings call for the quarter ended December 31, 2025, management said there are more competitive pressures now from private equity-backed roll-ups.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2025, management said PE-backed roll-ups have been cropping up everywhere over the last three years in particular and have been extremely aggressive in paying at higher and higher multiples.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, management contrasted its approach with competitors that are increasingly looking for an exit in three to five years or less, that compete with the largest check, and that change their comp plans every year to cross-sell more bank products.

The 2025 10-K states Raymond James competes directly with other national full-service broker-dealers, investment banking firms, commercial banks, investment advisors, investment managers and, to a lesser extent, discount brokers and dealers, and faces competition from more recent entrants including fintechs and increased use of alternative sales channels by other firms.

The 2025 10-K identifies the continued industry-wide trend in which financial advisors depart traditional firms to form independent RIAs or join third-party RIAs, some backed by private equity investors, as resulting in a highly competitive recruiting environment.
On the earnings call for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, management said private equity has certainly been competitive over the last 5 years, as well as some of the strategic firms.

On the earnings call for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, management said Raymond James does not lead with the highest check, and that in the absence of a true differentiated value proposition, the highest check is all a competitor has.

The 2025 10-K states Raymond James participates, with limited exceptions, in the Protocol for Broker Recruiting, notes that certain of its competitors may withdraw from it, and that companies in the industry frequently claim that competitors have engaged in unfair hiring practices when their employees or independent contractors accept positions with competitors.

Trade press (November 12, 2026) reports Raymond James will add $18.7 billion in client assets to its Financial Institutions Division, the unit dedicated to bank and credit union advisors, as an existing FID program merges with Synovus Financial Corp.; the advisors are expected to transition in May 2027. Why it might matter: the source states the deal merges Synovus Securities and Pinnacle Asset Management, Pinnacle Financial Partners' asset and wealth management arm.

Trade press (November 12, 2026) reports Raymond James will add 70 advisors to its Financial Institutions Division, the unit dedicated to bank and credit union advisors, as an existing FID program merges with Synovus Financial Corp.; the advisors are expected to transition in May 2027. Why it might matter: the source states the deal expands Pinnacle Financial Partners' relationship with Raymond James.
The 2025 10-K reports Raymond James had 3,693 employee financial advisors as of September 30, 2023.
The 2025 10-K reports Raymond James had 3,826 employee financial advisors as of September 30, 2024.
The 2025 10-K reports Raymond James had 3,878 employee financial advisors as of September 30, 2025.

The 2025 10-K reports Raymond James had 8,712 total financial advisors as of September 30, 2023.
The 2025 10-K reports Raymond James had 8,787 total financial advisors as of September 30, 2024.
The 2025 10-K reports Raymond James had 8,943 total financial advisors as of September 30, 2025.
The 2025 investor-day deck (published June 5, 2025) reports Raymond James had $332 billion of domestic PCG assets under administration in its employee affiliation model as of March 31, 2020.
The 2025 investor-day deck (published June 5, 2025) reports Raymond James had $631 billion of domestic PCG assets under administration in its employee affiliation model as of March 31, 2025.

The 2025 investor-day deck (published June 5, 2025) reports Raymond James had $318 billion of domestic PCG assets under administration in its independent contractor affiliation model as of March 31, 2020.

The 2025 investor-day deck (published June 5, 2025) reports Raymond James had $543 billion of domestic PCG assets under administration in its independent contractor affiliation model as of March 31, 2025.
The 2025 investor-day deck (published June 5, 2025) reports Raymond James had $46 billion of domestic PCG assets under administration in its RIA & Custody Services (RCS) model as of March 31, 2020.
The 2025 investor-day deck (published June 5, 2025) reports Raymond James had $186 billion of domestic PCG assets under administration in its RIA & Custody Services (RCS) model as of March 31, 2025.
The 2025 investor-day deck (published June 5, 2025) reports Raymond James had $696 billion of total domestic PCG assets under administration as of March 31, 2020.
The 2025 investor-day deck (published June 5, 2025) reports Raymond James had $1,360 billion of total domestic PCG assets under administration as of March 31, 2025.

Whether the mix across Raymond James affiliation models has shifted over time can be assessed on this evidence and the answer is yes, resting on management's own statements and the disclosed figures (with the metric definitions unverified). On the earnings call for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, CEO Paul Shoukry said that over the last year much more of the firm's recruiting has come from the independent side of the business versus the employee side, representing a mix shift, and clarified this mix shift was about the compensation ratio given the payout difference between the independent and employee channels. On the earnings call for the quarter ended September 30, 2024, CEO Paul Reilly said the RCS division has by far the highest percentage growth, that in total dollars a couple of years ago the independent channel led while this year the employee channel led, and that the old pattern of independents growing faster in down markets no longer holds. Trade press (October 29, 2026) reports the firm's recruiting success is spread across all its affiliation channels, with the independent contractor channel seeing the most interest in dollar volume and the RIA custody division growing at a high percentage rate on a smaller base. The disclosed domestic PCG assets under administration by model (2025 investor-day deck) show the employee model at $332 billion, the independent contractor model at $318 billion, and RCS at $46 billion as of March 31, 2020, versus $631 billion, $543 billion, and $186 billion respectively as of March 31, 2025.

a1.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes its advisor recruiting as part of a broader platform: recruits are interested in what the firm has been investing in, and recruiting occurs on the advisor-led side alongside flows coming in from workplace, with strength across all three channels.
items.quote: There's obviously a great platform. We have recruits that are interested in what we've been investing in. ... From the advisor-led side, we do have recruiting, but we also have flows coming in from workplace.

items.text: The firm states advisor recruitment remains strong, reflecting its reputation as an exceptional place where financial advisors can grow their businesses.
items.quote: Advisor recruitment remains strong, reflecting our reputation as an exceptional place where financial advisors can grow their businesses.

items.text: The firm describes that people are coming toward its platform and that financial advisors see the integrated firm as offering unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology, and compensation viewed as fair and motivating, while the firm remains selective and receives significant inbound inquiry.
items.quote: People are coming toward the platform. ... Folks want to come onto this platform. ... we can offer unique access to intellectual capital, world-class technology, compensation that is viewed to be fair and motivating ... we are selective about it ... Jed and Vince are getting a lot of inbound inquiry

items.text: Morgan Stanley grants employee loans under a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors.
items.quote: Employee loans are granted in conjunction with a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors, are full recourse and generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment with the Firm.

items.text: Morgan Stanley grants employee loans under a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors.
items.quote: Employee loans are granted in conjunction with a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors, are full recourse and generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment with the Firm.

items.text: The firm reports it is also seeing flows from the recruiting side on the advisor-led side of the business.
items.quote: On the advisor-led side, it is multiple clients and multiple different sections that you are actually seeing those flows come in, and we are also seeing flows from the recruiting side.

items.text: The firm notes that advisor-led asset flows come from both existing advisors and recruits, as well as from the origination of workplace relationships.
items.quote: Advisor-led is coming both from existing advisors as well as recruits and the origination of workplace.

a1.MS.reason: The passages describe Morgan Stanley's approach to advisor recruiting, including its platform, selective recruiting, reputation, use of employee loans, and sourcing of advisor-led flows from recruits.

a2.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley grants employee loans under a program 'established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors,' indicating it recruits certain financial advisors through transition loans.
items.quote: Employee loans are granted in conjunction with a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors, are full recourse and generally require periodic repayments

items.text: Morgan Stanley's advisor-led channel is sourced from both existing advisors and recruits (newly recruited advisors), as well as assets originating from the workplace channel.
items.quote: Advisor-led is coming both from existing advisors as well as recruits and the origination of workplace.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that advisor-led flows originated from new advisors who are attracted to the strength of the workplace offering.
items.quote: Advisor-led flows were particularly strong, originating from new advisors who are attracted to the strength of the workplace, as well as assets that originated from workplace.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is selective in its recruiting, but reports receiving significant inbound inquiry from advisors who want to join the platform.
items.quote: we are selective about it, but it is fair to say that Jed and Vince are getting a lot of inbound inquiry

items.text: Trade press reports Morgan Stanley seeks more of Barron's Top Advisors, indicating a focus on recruiting top (experienced) advisors.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley wants more Barron's Top Advisors so it poached Barron's 'Top Advisor' insiders

a2.MS.reason: The firm's disclosures describe recruiting 'certain Wealth Management financial advisors' via recruiting loans, recruits/new advisors as a source of advisor-led flows, and selective recruiting with strong inbound inquiry; trade press indicates targeting top advisors. No single passage fully specifies the breakdown of experienced vs. rookie vs. teams vs. breakaways, so these are partial facts.

a3.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley grants employee loans under a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors; the loans are full recourse, generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment.
items.quote: Employee loans are granted in conjunction with a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors, are full recourse and generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment with the Firm.

items.text: Morgan Stanley sought to claw back recruiting bonus money from a former advisor through promissory notes, loans that brokers pay back to firms over time.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley sued Cohen in 2021 in a dispute over promissory notes, loans that brokers pay back to firms over time. Morgan Stanley sought to claw back recruiting bonus money from Cohen.

items.text: Morgan Stanley sought to claw back $2.46 million in recruiting bonus loans, plus attorney's fees and interest, from a financial advisor.
items.quote: a sole FINRA arbitrator turned aside Morgan Stanley's attempt to claw back $2.46 million in recruiting bonus loans, along with attorney's fees and interest.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is not introducing retention bonuses as part of its 2027 pay plan for advisors; instead it is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses as part of their 2027 pay plans for advisors, adhering to a more traditional approach. As it has in the past, Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.

items.text: Morgan Stanley has taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue as deferred compensation, requiring advisors to stay for years in order to vest (referred to as golden handcuffs).
items.quote: Giants like Morgan Stanley for years have taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue, called it deferred compensation, and required advisors to stay for years in order to vest. If a financial advisor leaves a firm with a deferred compensation plan, he or she forfeits that compensation, which is also known on Wall Street as golden handcuffs.

a3.MS.reason: The passages describe the firm's recruiting/transition compensation, namely employee (recruiting) loans and promissory notes with clawback provisions, plus its 2027 pay-plan approach of increasing the pay threshold rather than adding retention bonuses, and deferred compensation tied to tenure.

a4.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley states that its deferred cash-based compensation (DCP) and stock-based compensation programs for financial advisors in Wealth Management generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions, which function to retain advisors by requiring continued employment to vest.
items.quote: The Firm sponsors a number of deferred cash-based compensation programs and stock-based compensation programs for current and former employees, including financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment, which generally contain vesting, clawback and cancellation provisions. Deferred compensation for financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.
items.definition: Deferred compensation for financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.

items.text: Morgan Stanley states its compensation programs reinforce values and culture through four key objectives, one of which is to attract and retain top talent; programs include annual bonuses, retirement savings plans with matching contributions, an employee stock purchase plan, student loan refinancing and a financial wellbeing program.

claims.text: Morgan Stanley: The 1Q26 10-Q (period ended March 31, 2026) and the 2025 10-K state that Wealth Management provides a comprehensive array of financial services and solutions to individual investors, including high and ultra-high net worth individuals, and businesses and institutions, and that it supports clients through three channels: Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace.

Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) describes its clients as high to ultra-high net worth individuals in the context of its U.S. Bank Subsidiaries' lending to customers, stating: "Our U.S. Bank Subsidiaries accept deposits, provide loans to a variety of customers, including large corporate and institutional clients, as well as high to ultra-high net worth individuals".

Merrill: The 2025 investor-day presentation (published November 5, 2025) describes a Wealth Continuum that segments clients into tiers including Mass Affluent ($500K - $1MM) and High Net Worth ($1MM - $10MM).

Merrill: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that Merrill Wealth Management's advisory business provides a high-touch client experience through a network of financial advisors focused on clients with over $250,000 in total investable assets.

Merrill: The 2025 investor-day presentation (published November 5, 2025) states that the Wealth Continuum allows it to deliver as one company and is its engine for lasting growth, reflecting its approach to serving clients across wealth tiers.
Merrill: As of September 30, 2026, Merrill defines its households as those with $250K+ in investable assets, excluding stock plan and banking-only households.
Merrill: As of September 30, 2026, Bank of America Private Bank defines its relationships as those with $3MM+ in total balances.
Merrill: The 2025 investor-day presentation (published November 5, 2025) reports households at a $500K+ asset threshold (750K such households).

Morgan Stanley: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) describes its Wealth Management clients as including 'high and ultra-high net worth individuals,' using 'high net worth' and 'ultra-high net worth' as its wealth-tier labels.

Morgan Stanley: The 2Q26 10-Q (period ended June 30, 2026) states that Wealth Management segments its clients by channel — Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace — rather than by named wealth tiers, and describes it as serving high and ultra-high net worth individuals.
Merrill: The 2025 investor-day presentation (published November 5, 2025) depicts a Wealth Continuum and labels the lowest shown tier 'Mass Affluent'.
Merrill: The 2025 investor-day presentation (published November 5, 2025) labels the next tier of its Wealth Continuum as 'High Net Worth'.

Merrill: Trade press reports (published September 8, 2026) use the label 'Merrill Private Wealth Management' for its business serving high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients, reporting that an advisor 'joins Merrill Private Wealth Management in McLean, Va., bringing about $1.2 billion in client assets from Morgan Stanley Private Wealth Management'.
Merrill: The 2025 investor-day materials (published November 5, 2025) refer to households of '$500K+' and '$10MM+' as wealth tiers within its client base.

Merrill: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that Bank of America Private Bank, together with Merrill Wealth Management's Private Wealth Management business, provides comprehensive wealth management solutions targeted to high net worth and ultra high net worth clients, as well as customized solutions to meet clients' wealth structuring, investment management, trust and banking needs.
Merrill: The 2025 investor-day presentation (published November 5, 2025) reports 750,000 households with $500,000 or more in assets (the '$500K+' wealth tier).
Merrill: The 2025 investor-day presentation (published November 5, 2025) reports 54,000 households with $10 million or more in assets (the '$10MM+' wealth tier).

Morgan Stanley and Merrill: On this evidence, the comparison is valid and the two firms differ in kind. Morgan Stanley organizes its Wealth Management clients through three channels — Advisor-Led, Self-Directed and Workplace — rather than through formal wealth tiers defined by asset breakpoints, and discloses no wealth thresholds or asset breakpoints defining its 'high and ultra-high net worth' tiers (2025 10-K). Merrill, by contrast, segments clients along a Wealth Continuum with named tiers and disclosed asset thresholds — Mass Affluent ($500K–$1MM) and High Net Worth ($1MM–$10MM), $500K+ and $10MM+ households, and a $250K+ threshold for its advisory business — and attaches differentiated service models to those tiers (2025 investor-day presentation and 2025 10-K).

claims.text: On this evidence the comparison can be made, and Merrill is unambiguously the most explicit: Merrill is the only firm that names a 'Mass Affluent' client segment, doing so in its Wealth Continuum, where the investor-day deck (November 2025) defines 'Mass Affluent ($500K - $1MM)'. Morgan Stanley names its clients only as 'individual investors, including high and ultra-high net worth individuals' and 'small to medium-sized businesses' and never uses the term for its own client base, while Raymond James names only 'high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth clients', a different and higher wealth tier. Schwab and Edward Jones have no statement naming a mass-affluent segment found in the documents searched.

a1.SCHW.label: fact

items.text: Schwab states that as one of the largest investment services firms in the U.S., its scale allows it to spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients, which keeps its costs low.
items.quote: Scale and Size of the Business - As one of the largest investment services firms in the U.S., we are able to spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients, and harness the resources to evolve capabilities to meet client needs.

items.text: Schwab states that coupled with scale, its operating efficiency and sharing of infrastructure across different businesses creates a cost advantage that enables it to competitively price products and services while profitably serving clients of various sizes across multiple channels.
items.quote: Coupled with scale, our operating efficiency and sharing of infrastructure across different businesses creates a cost advantage that enables us to competitively price products and services while profitably serving clients of various sizes across multiple channels.

items.text: Schwab states that its sheer scale, combined with efficiency efforts that make it easier for clients to do business with it, keeps its cost-to-serve clients low and allows it to invest in client capabilities that fuel growth.
items.quote: our sheer scale, combined with efficiency efforts that make it easier for clients to do business with us, keeps our cost-to-serve clients low. This also allows us to invest in client capabilities that will fuel our growth and fuel experiences that drive more efficiencies.

items.text: Schwab states that its scale, combined with expense discipline, has allowed it to decrease its cost per account by 20% over the last five years while remaining the industry leader on expense on client assets.
items.quote: Our scale, combined with our expense discipline, has allowed us to decrease our cost per account 20% over the last five years while driving our ability to remain the industry leader as measured by expense on client assets, or EOCA

items.text: Schwab states that its marketing spend drives approximately 40% of new-to-firm retail clients.
items.quote: We are investing in our marketing spend, which drives approximately 40% of new-to-firm retail clients.

items.text: Schwab states that marketing is a core growth engine for consistent client and asset growth, and that its data and insight-led model drives efficiency at scale.
items.quote: 1 Marketing is a core growth engine for consistent client & asset growth 2 Our data & insight-led model drives efficiency at scale

items.text: Schwab states that its marketing mix optimization model increased ad spend efficiency by 15% from 2021 to 2025.
items.quote: 15% Increasing Ad Spend Efficiency 2 2021 - 2025

items.text: Schwab states that management couples Schwab's scale and resources with ongoing expense discipline to keep costs low and ensure products and solutions are affordable.
items.quote: management works to couple Schwab's scale and resources with ongoing expense discipline to keep costs low and ensure that products and solutions are affordable as well as responsive to client needs.

a1.SCHW.reason: Multiple passages state how Schwab's scale spreads costs, creates a cost advantage, keeps cost-to-serve low, and improves marketing efficiency to cheaply acquire clients; all are direct statements attributed to Schwab.

claims.text: The Charles Schwab Corporation: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that as one of the largest investment services firms in the U.S., its scale allows it to spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients, which keeps its costs low: "Scale and Size of the Business - As one of the largest investment services firms in the U.S., we are able to spread operating costs and amortize new investments over a large base of clients, and harness the resources to evolve capabilities to meet client needs."

The Charles Schwab Corporation: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that coupled with scale, its operating efficiency and sharing of infrastructure across different businesses creates a cost advantage that enables it to competitively price products and services while profitably serving clients of various sizes across multiple channels: "Coupled with scale, our operating efficiency and sharing of infrastructure across different businesses creates a cost advantage that enables us to competitively price products and services while profitably serving clients of various sizes across multiple channels."

The Charles Schwab Corporation: On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), Schwab stated that its sheer scale, combined with efficiency efforts that make it easier for clients to do business with it, keeps its cost-to-serve clients low and allows it to invest in client capabilities that fuel growth: "our sheer scale, combined with efficiency efforts that make it easier for clients to do business with us, keeps our cost-to-serve clients low. This also allows us to invest in client capabilities that will fuel our growth and fuel experiences that drive more efficiencies."

The Charles Schwab Corporation: On the 4Q25 earnings call (January 2026), Schwab stated that its scale, combined with expense discipline, has allowed it to decrease its cost per account by 20% over the last five years while remaining the industry leader as measured by expense on client assets: "Our scale, combined with our expense discipline, has allowed us to decrease our cost per account 20% over the last five years while driving our ability to remain the industry leader as measured by expense on client assets, or EOCA."

Edward Jones: The 2025 10-K (period ended December 31, 2025) states that Edward Jones targets new clients through three initiatives: High Net Worth (focused on attracting and serving high net worth clients through expanded advice, planning, products and services across multiple service models); Workplace (which connects local business owners and their employees with financial solutions through their workplace); and a new digital platform (focused on attracting and retaining Next Generation investors).

a1.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley describes a 'funnel' strategy in which the workplace channel serves as the top of the funnel, bringing relationships and assets onto the platform that the firm then works to deepen into advice-based, advisor-led and fee-based relationships.
items.quote: illustrating the strength of the workplace channel as a strong contributor to the top of the funnel. With strong capital markets, the power of our client acquisition funnel is becoming increasingly evident. Workplace brings relationships and assets onto the platform, and we are well positioned to support these new relationships.

items.text: The firm describes the conversion as a two-step funnel: first retaining assets that vest in the workplace channel, then over time driving 'channel migration' where those workplace assets seek advice and move into the advisor-led channel, supported by technology and investment.
items.quote: The first is we retain those assets... And then over time... we are seeing channel migration, and that's with technology and investment, where those Workplace assets are now actually seeking advice and that migration is something that has helped to contribute to over $1 trillion of total assets in our adviser-led strategy.

items.text: The firm describes attachment points that bring clients to E*TRADE in the corporate stock plan (workplace) context, and then, where appropriate, fee-based flows that make their way to advisers.
items.quote: we are very excited about the attachment points ultimately that bring clients to E*TRADE, that we are close with them in the corporate stock plan context, i.e., workplace, but then ultimately, where it's appropriate, fee-based flows that make their way to the advisers

items.text: The firm defines advisor-led flows from workplace as assets brought into advisor-led relationships where the initial account was workplace or self-directed.
items.quote: Advisor-Led Flows from Workplace and E*TRADE represent assets brought into advisor-led relationships, where the initial account was workplace or self-directed.
items.definition: Advisor-Led Flows from Workplace and E*TRADE represent assets brought into advisor-led relationships, where the initial account was workplace or self-directed.

a1.MS.reason: The passages describe the firm's stated strategy of a workplace-led client acquisition funnel that retains assets and migrates them into advisor-led, fee-based relationships, which is exactly what the sub-question asks for.

a3.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley invests in building referral models and products like LeadIQ that match workplace individuals with advisers.
items.quote: They're going into creating our referral models. They're going into products like LeadIQ that will allow us to match individuals with advisers.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's relationship with Carta operates as a referral-based model, referring private companies to Morgan Stanley as they move from the private to public side.
items.quote: The original relationship started as a referral-based model. As companies began to move from a private side to a public side, they would be referred to Morgan Stanley.

items.text: Morgan Stanley has an exclusive partnership with Carta through which Carta refers private companies' stock plans to Morgan Stanley as they go public.
items.quote: we have an exclusive partnership with Carta, which means that they will refer those private different stock plans or different corporate companies to Morgan Stanley as they move into going public.

a4.MS.label: fact

items.quote: LeadIQ, our AI-powered lead distribution platform, focusing on matching workplace and self-directed relationships and facilitating engagement with our financial advisors.

items.text: For workplace participants who do not yet have an advice-based relationship, Morgan Stanley works a referral model that can begin as early as financial education, including with 401(k) assets, to help people understand where they could use advice.

And that's something that can begin as early as the financial education spot, and it can also begin -- like I said, we have examples with 401(k)s and new 401(k) assets that come in that is not necessarily an IPO-specific workplace where we're really giving people that ability to better understand where they could use advice.

items.text: Morgan Stanley invests in creating referral models and products like LeadIQ to match individuals with advisers, with the goal of being their principal financial adviser.
items.quote: They're going into creating our referral models. They're going into products like LeadIQ that will allow us to match individuals with advisers. And our goal is to be their principal financial adviser.
