a3.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley's Integrated Firm delivers capabilities throughout clients' growth cycles, including 'Founders Wealth Strategies' and 'Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning' to help clients 'Preserve Wealth,' which serve founders and support the transfer and preservation of wealth.
items.quote: Founders / Employees ... Invest for the Future ... Financial Wellness and Employee Benefits ... Founders Wealth Strategies ... Preserve Wealth ... Full-Service Wealth Advice and Asset Allocation ... Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning

items.text: Morgan Stanley retains 99% of its clients, and 60% of advisor-led assets are associated with clients who have an average relationship duration of 20 years, reflecting their enduring trust in Morgan Stanley.
items.quote: 60% of advisor-led assets are associated with clients who have an average duration of 20 years. We retain 99% of our clients, reflecting their enduring trust in Morgan Stanley.

a3.MS.reason: Passages state Morgan Stanley's wealth-transfer and preservation capabilities (family office solutions, trust & estate planning, founders wealth strategies) and its multi-decade client retention, addressing how it retains assets and relationships across the wealth lifecycle and generations.

a4.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley takes a portion of an advisor's gross revenue as deferred compensation that requires advisors to stay for years in order to vest, a retention mechanism known as 'golden handcuffs.'
items.quote: Giants like Morgan Stanley for years have taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue, called it deferred compensation, and required advisors to stay for years in order to vest. If a financial advisor leaves a firm with a deferred compensation plan, he or she forfeits that compensation, which is also known on Wall Street as golden handcuffs.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is not introducing retention bonuses in its 2027 pay plan for advisors, and is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses as part of their 2027 pay plans for advisors, adhering to a more traditional approach. As it has in the past, Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.

items.text: Morgan Stanley identifies its ability to retain and attract qualified employees and successfully transition key roles as critical to its business, a risk factor touching on talent succession.
items.quote: If we are unable to continue to attract, integrate and retain highly qualified employees or successfully transition key roles, or do so at levels or in forms necessary to maintain our competitive position, our performance, including our competitive position and results of operations, could be materially adversely affected.

a4.MS.reason: Passages describe MS's advisor retention approach (deferred compensation, no retention bonuses, 10% pay threshold increase) and a talent-transition risk factor relevant to an aging advisor force, though no specific succession/retirement program is disclosed.

a5.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley's integrated firm delivers capabilities across clients' growth cycle, from founders/employees and early-stage through public company, including financial wellness and employee benefits, founders wealth strategies, full-service wealth advice and asset allocation, family office solutions and trust & estate planning, private shares trading & lending, and IPO execution and support services.
items.quote: Founders / Employees ... Early Stage ... Public Company ... Invest for the Future ... Financial Wellness and Employee Benefits ... Founders Wealth Strategies ... Preserve Wealth ... Full-Service Wealth Advice and Asset Allocation ... Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning ... Unlock Liquidity ... Private Shares Trading & Lending ... IPO Execution and Support Services ... Optimize for Growth

items.text: Morgan Stanley is using its scale to invest in broadening capabilities for financial advisors that are difficult for others to replicate, including alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.
items.quote: We are using our scale to invest in broadening capabilities for FAs that are difficult for others to replicate: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

items.text: Morgan Stanley offers advice-based services to founders and family offices and works to service private companies through its expanded collaboration with Carta, and partners with Zero Hash in digital assets.
items.quote: We're offering our advice-based service to those individuals ... We've done a lot of work on trying to service founders, on trying to service family offices.

items.text: Morgan Stanley's strategic initiatives for innovation include its recent acquisition of EquityZen, expanded partnership with Carta, and collaboration with Zero Hash, laying the foundation for growth to widen competitive moats.
items.quote: Strategic initiatives such as our recent acquisition of EquityZen, expanded partnership with Carta, and collaboration with Zero Hash all reflect our commitment to innovation.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is offering new private-market products to clients, such as evergreen products and products that allow for lower denomination size, as part of a more democratized alternatives offering for its retail client base.
items.quote: We're offering new products to our clients, such as evergreen products and products that allow for lower denomination size.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is working on products to fill gaps and help provide a more democratized alternatives offering to its retail client base, given roughly 5% of qualified assets are in private alternatives versus a recommendation closer to 15%.
items.quote: we are looking also at places to help fill these gaps and to help you provide a more democratized offering.

items.text: The workplace channel includes equity compensation solutions for companies, their executives and employees (stock plan administration), serving as a channel to attract and serve next-generation clients.
items.quote: The workplace channel includes equity compensation solutions for companies, their executives and employees.

items.text: Morgan Stanley offers financial advice and financial wellness to clients and matches advisers to clients using its technology, bringing clients into its client-acquisition funnel across the self-directed, workplace and adviser-led channels.
items.quote: what kind of financial advice and financial wellness can you offer to the clients ... we have a greater ability to match advisers to the right clients with all the technology that we've put into place.

items.text: Morgan Stanley continues to invest in its self-directed E*TRADE platform and expand its workplace channel as an engine for future growth, alongside the client acquisition funnel that spans workplace, self-directed and adviser-led channels.
items.quote: a build-out of E*TRADE capabilities, and the expansion of our essential workplace channel, serve as an engine for future growth.

a5.MS.reason: Multiple passages describe Morgan Stanley's products, services and platforms for attracting and serving next-generation clients (workplace/stock plan, founders, family office, private markets, digital assets).

a6.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley's strategic update deck lists "Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning" among the capabilities the Integrated Firm delivers to clients in the "Preserve Wealth" stage of their growth cycle, reflecting engagement with families and multi-generational wealth planning.
items.quote: Preserve Wealth / Full-Service Wealth Advice and Asset Allocation / Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning

items.text: The same deck shows the Integrated Firm serving clients across a lifecycle from founders/employees through early stage to public company, with offerings including "Founders Wealth Strategies," "Financial Wellness and Employee Benefits," and "Full-Service Wealth Advice and Asset Allocation."
items.quote: Founders / Employees / Early Stage / Public Company / Invest for the Future / Financial Wellness and Employee Benefits / Founders Wealth Strategies / Preserve Wealth / Full-Service Wealth Advice and Asset Allocation

items.text: A Morgan Stanley strategic update slide lists "Family Office, OCIO, Tailored Lending" among its offerings for clients.
items.quote: Family Office, OCIO, Tailored Lending

items.text: CEO Ted Pick highlighted that Morgan Stanley offers "ultra-high net worth family office infrastructure solutions" as part of the differentiated products and capabilities available to clients.
items.quote: You have access to private markets via equities, you have co-investment opportunities and then importantly, for ultra-high net worth family office infrastructure solutions.

items.text: CEO Ted Pick said the firm is using its scale to invest in broadening capabilities for financial advisors including "family office and OCIO, and tailored lending."
items.quote: alternatives and privates, tax-efficient investing, digitized assets, family office and OCIO, and tailored lending.

items.text: CFO Sharon Yeshaya said the firm has "done a lot of work on trying to service founders, on trying to service family offices" as part of growing its Wealth Management coverage of individual clients.
items.quote: We've done a lot of work on trying to service founders, on trying to service family offices.

items.text: CEO Ted Pick said Morgan Stanley's scaled capabilities and business mix "can support our clients throughout an entire life cycle," citing Morgan Stanley at Work as positioning the firm as an early trusted advisor to private companies.
items.quote: We have scaled capabilities and a business mix that can support our clients throughout an entire life cycle.

a6.MS.reason: Multiple passages describe Morgan Stanley's family office, trust and estate planning, founders, and full-lifecycle capabilities that engage families and facilitate multi-generational wealth planning.

a7.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley's strategic deck ("Why Morgan Stanley Wins: The Integrated Firm Delivers Unmatched Capabilities Throughout Clients Growth Cycles") presents capabilities to serve founders and employees through their growth cycles, listing "Founders Wealth Strategies," "Preserve Wealth," "Full-Service Wealth Advice and Asset Allocation," and "Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning" among its offerings.
items.quote:
Founders Wealth Strategies

Preserve Wealth

Full-Service Wealth Advice and Asset Allocation

Family Office Solutions, Trust & Estate Planning

items.text: CEO Ted Pick stated Morgan Stanley formalized the integrated firm by positioning leadership talent at the center of client coverage to drive growth as the firm serves more clients across their full suite of needs.
items.quote: we have formalized the integrated firm by positioning leadership talent at the center of client coverage, integrated data, risk management, and infrastructure to drive growth as we serve more clients across their full suite of needs

items.text: CEO Ted Pick described Morgan Stanley's four pillars supporting the integrated firm, framing strategy as consistently serving clients in raising, managing, and allocating capital, and growth as smart strategic investments that generate new opportunities to capture client share.
items.quote: Strategy is about consistently serving our clients in raising, managing, and allocating capital. Culture is about rigor, humility, and partnership. Financial strength is about strong capital and liquidity alongside durable earnings, and growth is about smart, strategic investments across the firm, which generate new opportunities to capture client share.

a7.MS.reason: The strategic deck explicitly lists trust & estate planning, family office solutions, and founders wealth strategies, and CEO statements describe the integrated firm serving clients holistically to capture client share, indicating commitment to wealth transfer.

a8.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley defines net new assets (NNA) as client asset inflows, inclusive of interest, dividends and asset acquisitions, less client asset outflows, excluding the impact of business combinations/divestitures and the impact of fees and commissions.
items.quote: NNA represent client asset inflows, inclusive of interest, dividends and asset acquisitions, less client asset outflows, and exclude the impact of business combinations/divestitures and the impact of fees and commissions.
items.definition: NNA represent client asset inflows, inclusive of interest, dividends and asset acquisitions, less client asset outflows, and exclude the impact of business combinations/divestitures and the impact of fees and commissions.

claims.text: Raymond James Financial: As of September 30, 2025 (whole firm), Raymond James had approximately 19,500 associates, including 3,878 employee financial advisors and 5,065 independent advisors.

Whether client assets per advisor can be validly compared across the five firms: not valid on this evidence. The client asset measures differ — Morgan Stanley's Total Client Assets sum Wealth Management client assets and Investment Management AuM, with certain WM client assets also counted in IM AuM (double-counted); Schwab's total client assets span self-directed, RIA custodial, workplace, and banking relationships; Edward Jones reports assets under care; Merrill discloses GWIM AUM (which includes Bank of America Private Bank) or Merrill-only AUM; and Raymond James reports assets under administration. The advisor denominators also differ — Morgan Stanley's Wealth Management representatives differ from its broader Form ADV registered-representative count; Schwab discloses no financial advisor headcount (only employee/FTE counts); Edward Jones reports financial advisors (spanning U.S. and Canada); Merrill's disclosed wealth advisor counts span GWIM plus Consumer Banking; and Raymond James excludes RCS-division advisors from its count even though their client assets are included in AUA, a numerator/denominator mismatch. Separately, client assets per advisor is not in the metric definitions file (unverified), so the per-advisor figures are not comparable across firms.

a1.MS.label: fact

items.text: Morgan Stanley discloses that compensation for its Wealth Management advisors is paid on a formulaic payout basis linked to compensable revenue, and that increases in compensation expense are driven by this formulaic payout on higher revenues.
items.quote: primarily due to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors driven by higher compensable revenue

items.text: For certain revenue-producing employees in the Wealth Management and Investment Management business segments, compensation is largely paid on the basis of formulaic payouts that link employee compensation to revenues.
items.quote: For certain revenue-producing employees in the Wealth Management and Investment Management business segments, compensation is largely paid on the basis of formulaic payouts that link employee compensation to revenues.

items.text: Deferred compensation for financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.
items.quote: Deferred compensation for financial advisors in the Wealth Management business segment is generally composed of 75% cash-based awards and 25% stock-based awards.

items.text: The amount of the fee a client pays is a factor used in calculating the compensation paid to the Financial Advisor, and if the fee rate is below a certain threshold the advisor is given credit for less than the total amount of the fee.
items.quote: The amount of the fee you pay is a factor we use in calculating the compensation we pay your Financial Advisor... If your fee rate is below a certain threshold, we give your Financial Advisor credit for less than the total amount of your fee in calculating his or her compensation.

items.text: A Morgan Stanley Virtual Advisor (MSVA) is paid a base salary plus a discretionary bonus and does not retain any portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee.
items.quote: your MSVA is paid a base salary plus a discretionary bonus and does not retain any portion of the Morgan Stanley Advisory Fee.

items.text: Morgan Stanley announced it will increase the cash component of its advisor compensation, stating the changes support its investment in financial advisors and simplify its compensation program.
items.quote: As previously announced, we will also increase the cash component of our advisor compensation... these changes support our overall investment into our financial advisors and will help simplify our compensation program.

items.text: In the first quarter of 2026, the Firm reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management advisors.
items.quote: in the first quarter of 2026, the Firm reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management advisors.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.

items.text: Compensation and benefits expenses include base salaries and fixed allowances, formulaic programs, discretionary incentive compensation, amortization of deferred cash and equity awards, changes in the fair value of DCP investments, carried interest, severance costs, and other items such as health and welfare benefits.
items.quote: Compensation and benefits expenses include base salaries and fixed allowances, formulaic programs, discretionary incentive compensation, amortization of deferred cash and equity awards, changes in the fair value of the referenced notional DCP investments, carried interest allocated to employees, severance costs, and other items such as health and welfare benefits.

a1.MER.label: not_found
a1.MER.reason: The passages mention Merrill's co-presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf and regional leaders, but only reference leadership roles assumed before 2026 (e.g., co-presidents took over in 2023, Nathan Marsden in June 2023); no leadership or management-structure change occurring since the start of 2026 is stated.

a2.MER.label: fact

items.text: Merrill created two new kinds of fees for third-party asset managers: a data analytics fee and a negotiable revenue-sharing 'support fee,' effective January 1, 2027.
items.quote: Two kinds of fees have been newly created. Third-party managers can buy as much as $1.4 million worth of "incentives" per annum through one fee, by maxing out data analytics buys. The second fee is a basis points revenue share that can cost asset managers as much as 0.1% on all Merill assets they manage. ... the Bank of America subsidiary is making it possible to pay more to get more visibility and middleman love, effective, Jan. 1, 2027.

items.text: Merrill's new data analytics fees will cost asset managers between $125,000 and $860,000 per firm per year for data on actively managed products, and between $25,000 and $550,000 for data on passive ETFs.
items.quote: Merrill's new data analytics fees will cost asset managers between $125,000 and $860,000 per-firm, per-year for data on actively managed products, including ETFs, mutual funds, annuities and model portfolios. Data on passive ETFs managed through Merrill's platforms will cost between $25,000 and $550,000.

items.text: Merrill's new negotiable revenue-sharing 'support fee' will cost up to $1 million for every $1 billion of funds an asset manager manages on behalf of Merrill advisors, with fees ranging from 0.02% to a maximum of 0.1%.
items.quote: Its new "negotiable" revenue-sharing "support fee" will cost up to $1 million, for every $1 billion of funds an asset manager manages on behalf of Merrill advisors, with fees ranging from 0.02% on high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth assets, to a maximum 0.1% on third party mutual funds, money market funds, and active ETFs.

items.text: Merrill launched two new services, Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) and Dollar Cost Averaging Service (DCA), to help clients implement tax-efficient transitions and systematic cash deployment within personalized investment strategies.
items.quote: Merrill today announced the launch of Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) and Dollar Cost Averaging Service (DCA), new services that combine automation with professional portfolio oversight to help clients simplify asset transitions and cash deployment into managed or custom managed investment strategies in the Merrill Lynch Investment Advisory Program (IAP).

items.text: Merrill has returned to veteran broker recruiting, having largely pulled back from it at the end of 2017, with recruited assets to the wealth unit doubling year-over-year as of October.
items.quote: Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm has returned to veteran broker recruiting. The firm largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017 but returned after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf, who took over in 2023, restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer.

items.text: Merrill executives said the firm would continue to invest in AI and digital capabilities, and Merrill's president and co-head noted client sales of alternative investments increased 19% in the quarter.
items.quote: While the Merrill executive did not mention new AI tools, the message was clear that the firm would continue to invest in AI and digital capabilities. ... At Merrill Lynch, client sales of alternative investments increased 19% in the quarter, said Eric Schimpf, president and co-head of Merrill Wealth Management.

a2.MER.reason: Passages describe new initiatives (data/support fees, TET/DCA services), a strategic change (return to veteran broker recruiting), and continued investment in AI/digital and alternatives, all within 2026.

a3.MER.reason: The passages state Merrill/Bank of America's net advisor loss of 552 through Aug 13, 2026, which is the change in advisor headcount since the start of the year.
